$note: How a release is decided here: release-please reads the conventional commits on main since the last
tag, opens a pull request that bumps package.json and writes CHANGELOG.md, and MERGING that pull
request is what cuts the tag and the GitHub release. `.github/workflows/release.yml` is what the
published GitHub release then starts: it packs, consumes and publishes to npm. Nothing else publishes.
ONE PACKAGE, AT THE ROOT, AND THE TAG HAS NO COMPONENT: `v0.1.0`, not `vscode-webview-kit-v0.1.0`.
release.yml refuses any tag that is not exactly `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, so a prefixed tag would
publish nothing, loudly. This is the sidecar's shape (one product, `v*`), not the four-component one.
$bootstrap: THE FIRST RELEASE IS 0.1.0, and getting there needs two settings that only work together. Measured
against release-please 17.x as bundled by release-please-action v5.0.0 (dist/index.js), not recalled:
1. The manifest is EMPTY (`{}`). When no release is found for a path but the manifest names a version
other than 0.0.0, release-please logs 'No latest release found ... but a previous version (X) was
specified in the manifest' and treats X as ALREADY RELEASED - so a manifest saying 0.1.0 would cut
0.1.1 or 0.2.0, and 0.1.0 would never exist. That is how the siblings bootstrapped (their manifests
name versions that WERE tagged); this package has no tag yet, so the sibling shape is wrong here.
2. `initial-version` is 0.1.0. With no previous release, `buildNewVersion` returns
`initialReleaseVersion()`, which is `initial-version` when set and otherwise 1.0.0 - the node
strategy does not override it (rust, python and others answer 0.1.0; node does not).
After 0.1.0 is tagged, release-please writes `{".": "0.1.0"}` into the manifest itself and
`initial-version` is never read again. `src/test/releaseConfig.test.ts` holds both states against
package.json, so a manifest that names an unreleased version fails the suite.
$sections: THE CHANGELOG SECTIONS ARE ALSO WHAT DECIDES WHETHER A RELEASE OPENS. release-please skips a release
whose notes would be empty, so a VISIBLE section is a releasing type. Visible: feat, fix, perf and
revert - exactly the types `.github/scripts/docs-only-title.mjs` treats as releasing. Every other type
pr-title.yml accepts is listed and hidden, so `docs:`, `test:`, `ci:`, `chore:`, `refactor:` and
`build:` never open a release on their own. `src/test/releaseConfig.test.ts` derives both lists
$exclude: A COMMIT THAT TOUCHES NOTHING BUT `.github` IS NOT A RELEASE (the family's measured lesson,
2026-09-21: `feat(ci):` on a workflow-only change proposed a minor release of unchanged code three
times). An exclude path is a DIRECTORY PREFIX (`isRelevant` is `file.indexOf(path + '/') === 0`), so
only a directory belongs here; and a commit touching `.github` AND anything else is still released.
$draft: NOT A DRAFT, unlike the siblings, and on purpose. Their releases carry ASSETS that are uploaded after
the tag, so a public release would sit empty; this one carries none - the artefact is on npm. A
published (non-draft) release is what raises `release: published`, the one event release.yml listens
to; a draft raises nothing until a person publishes it.
